metaDescription: Five nugget ice makers at or under $400, including 80 to 100 pound undercounter bins and a 44 pound countertop unit, compared on storage, output and plumbing.
expertTake: The 100 pound undercounter unit with a 25 pound bin and dual water inlet is the pick because it pairs the biggest output with the most flexible water supply. The Euhomy 80 pound stainless unit is the value choice for a steadier, smaller bin. Anyone who needs only a few cups of ice a day should skip undercounter machines and stay with a countertop model.
introParagraphs: Past the countertop tier, nugget machines add something new: an insulated bin that holds a day's ice and a drain or pump that handles meltwater. That turns an appliance you refill every hour into one you check once a day.

Prices drift, and the $400 cap used here reflects Amazon listing prices when this guide was updated. The budget is large enough to reach 80 to 100 pound freestanding units, so the decisions become bin size, water source and how much counter or floor space you can commit.

products.name: 100 lb Undercounter Nugget Ice Maker with Dual Water Inlet
products.description:
This freestanding unit lists 100 pounds a day with a 25 pound capacity and a 20 pound insulated storage bin, the largest in the lineup. The headline feature is the dual water inlet, which accepts both a reservoir fill and a bottled-water jug up to 5 gallons, so it can sit where there is no plumbing. A powerful compressor does the heavy lifting.

Against the Costway 90 pound unit, it makes a little more ice and has the bigger bin, which matters for a party. Set beside the Euhomy 80 pound, it gives you more output but less polished controls. The dual inlet is the real flexibility edge, because most undercounter machines expect a hose or a water line that a rental kitchen does not have.

Living with it means managing water supply and drain. Keep the jug supply near the machine, and empty the drain tray if the unit lacks a pump. Descale every month or two if your water is hard, and leave room for the compressor to breathe on all sides. When the jug runs low the machine can run dry and shut down, so keep a spare full bottle beside it, and sanitize the jug neck whenever you swap bottles because a dirty neck puts bacteria straight into the ice path. Level the cabinet feet before the first run, since a tilted unit fills the bin unevenly.
products.bestFor: Entertainers and small offices that want a large bin without plumbing.
pros: 100 lb per day, the highest rating here
cons: Large footprint on a counter or floor
Auger noise is louder than a bullet maker

products.name: 100 lb Undercounter Nugget Ice Machine with 24-Hour Timer
products.description:
This unit also lists 100 pounds a day, and adds a 24-hour timer that lets you schedule production so a full bin is waiting in the morning. The listing frames the output as more than 5,000 nuggets, enough for over 400 drinks. A Clean button starts an automatic wash, so maintenance is one press.

It competes directly with the dual-inlet 100 pounder, and the timer is the differentiator: you can run it overnight when the house is quiet and electricity use is low. What it does not list is a clear bin capacity, so check the listing for storage details before you plan around it. Measured against the Euhomy 80 pound, it offers more output but a less detailed control panel.

Set the timer to finish an hour before you need ice, because a freshly made bin is soft and clumps if it melts. Use filtered water, and run the wash cycle monthly. A rubber mat under the feet helps with vibration noise.
products.bestFor: Households that want ice ready on a schedule.
cons: Bin capacity less clear on the listing

products.name: COSTWAY 90 lb Commercial-Style Nugget Ice Maker
products.description:
The Costway rates 90 pounds a day into a 15 pound storage bin. Pressing and holding the ON/OFF button for three seconds starts the self-cleaning function, a simple procedure that helps users who forget maintenance. The ice is the same soft, chewable pellet style as the others, and it is marketed for gatherings or daily use.

The 15 pound bin is the limiting number: it stops production when full and the ice slowly melts, so a 90 pound daily rating needs regular use to be realized. Against the 100 pound units it makes about ten percent less ice and has a smaller bin, but it is also a less expensive machine. Next to the Euhomy 80 pound unit, it has a higher rating and similar bin.

Care is routine. Clean the bin and scoop, descale on schedule, and keep the drain clear. Because the build is commercial-style, expect a heavier machine than a countertop model, and plan to move it only with the bin empty.
products.bestFor: Families that want a bigger bin but not the highest price tier.
pros: 15 lb bin holds a day of drinks
cons: Bin is smaller than the 25 lb unit

products.name: EUHOMY 80 lb Stainless Undercounter Nugget Ice Maker
products.description:
The Euhomy 80 pounder has a built-in 15 pound bin and a multifunction LCD that shows ambient conditions and ice status. Output is rated at 80 pounds a day, below the other undercounter picks, and the stainless body is easier to wipe than plastic. The panel is the most informative in the lineup, which helps you spot a fault before the bin runs empty.

Next to the Costway, it gives up ten pounds of output for a nicer shell and better readout. Set beside the 100 pound units, it trades about a fifth of the volume for a calmer feel and likely quieter running at lower production. It is the right size for a household that goes through a bin a day rather than two.

Keep the stainless clean with a soft cloth, and descale on a monthly rhythm. Use the LCD to confirm the bin is not full before assuming a fault. Let the machine rest upright after any move so compressor oil settles.
products.bestFor: Households that want a tidy stainless bin machine with clear feedback.
pros: 80 lb per day is enough for most homes
cons: Lowest output of the undercounter picks
Bin matches the Costway rather than the larger unit

products.name: EUHOMY 44 lb Countertop Nugget Ice Maker, Black
products.description:
The only countertop machine in this lineup, it rates 44 pounds a day and starts first ice in 7 to 10 minutes. It has no storage bin to speak of, so it suits people who want constant fresh ice rather than a day's supply. The single ICE button keeps use simple.

It is far less ice than the undercounter units, but it needs no drain, no jug and no floor space. Measured against the Euhomy 80 pound unit, it loses about half the output and the stainless body, but it also costs less to place and run. For a small household that only wants chewable ice on tap, this is plenty.

Filter the water and descale monthly in hard-water areas. Give the machine 6 inches of space on every side, and keep it away from a hot stove. Wipe the basket when you are done and empty the reservoir if you leave for a few days.
products.bestFor: Small households that want nugget ice without plumbing or floor space.
pros: No drain or floor space needed
cons: Much less ice than undercounter units
Basket does not store a day of ice

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 100 pound daily rating means little if the bin holds 15 pounds, because production stops when the bin is full. The 25 pound unit with a 20 pound insulated bin carries a day's worth for a crowd, while the Costway and Euhomy 15 pound bins fit a household that empties one bin a day. Think of the bin as your buffer: size it to your busiest evening, not the average day. Nugget ice also settles and clumps as it sits, so a deep bin that is mostly full gets harder to scoop cleanly from the bottom. If you only occasionally host, the smaller 15 pound bin refilled across an afternoon matches real use better than a huge reserve you pay to keep cold.

Undercounter machines make meltwater that has to go somewhere. Some use a drain line or a pump, and others recycle water to a reservoir. The dual-inlet 100 pounder accepts a bottled jug up to 5 gallons, so it needs no plumbing for water supply. Plan the drain route before you buy, since a floor drain or sink nearby saves effort every week.

A freestanding undercounter unit is heavier and wider than a countertop machine. It needs ventilation on its sides and back, so do not wedge it between cabinets without checking the manual. The 44 pound countertop model avoids this by sitting on a counter, which is a point for small kitchens. Measure door swing and cord reach before ordering.

The Euhomy 80 pound has an LCD that shows ambient conditions, while the timer-equipped 100 pounder lets you schedule production. A control panel that tells you the bin is full saves you from troubleshooting a machine that is working fine. Prefer clear indicators over a single button when the bin matters.

Undercounter machines have more interior surface than countertop ones, so a self-clean function is a must. The Costway starts a cycle with a three-second hold and the timer unit has a Clean button. A cycle still does not dissolve scale, so descale with an approved cleaner every one to two months in hard water. Pull the scoop and keep it in a clean container rather than leaving it in the bin, since a scoop resting in nugget ice grows a film within days. If the ice ever smells musty, the bin and drain are the first places to check, long before the compressor.

Larger compressors and augers are louder, and an undercounter machine in an open kitchen will be heard. A rubber mat under the feet reduces the vibration that carries through floors. Schedule production overnight with a timer if the machine is near living space, though a bedroom wall behind the unit will carry the freeze-cycle thump straight into your sleep. Expect a freeze-cycle hum with periodic dropping sounds as nuggets fall into the bin.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum rated output in cool conditions. Real output drops in warm rooms and with warm incoming water.
specDecoder.watchFor: Both 100 pound units list this figure, but neither guarantees it in a hot garage.

specDecoder.meaning: The amount of ice the machine can store before production stops. Insulation slows melting but does not freeze ice.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 25 pound unit lists a 20 pound insulated bin, and the others list 15 pounds.

specDecoder.meaning: A design that accepts either a fill reservoir or a bottled jug. It removes the need for a plumbed water line.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the first-ranked unit lists a 5-gallon jug inlet.

specDecoder.meaning: A schedule that tells the machine when to run. It can shift noise and electricity use to off-peak times.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check the timer unit's bin size before relying on it for a party.

specDecoder.meaning: A button or hold command that starts a rinse cycle. It does not replace descaling.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Costway's three-second hold is easy to forget, so set a monthly reminder.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: Rated output and bin size were weighed together, from 100 pounds with a 25 pound capacity to a 44 pound countertop machine with a minimal basket. A big rating with a small bin scored lower than a balanced pair.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water supply flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each machine receives water and deals with meltwater. The dual-inlet 100 pounder scored highest for flexibility, and the countertop Euhomy scored for needing no plumbing at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and cleaning
howWeEvaluated.description: LCD feedback, timers and self-clean buttons were compared. The Euhomy LCD and the 24-hour timer stood out, while the three-second Costway hold scored for simplicity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: Stainless, plastic and commercial-style bodies were compared for weight and wipe-down ease. A 44 pound countertop model was scored for its small footprint.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every item is at or under the cap on its live listing. We favored models that spend the higher budget on storage and output instead of one that adds only styling.

rows: Higher output at a modest premium

cards.label: Countertop (EUHOMY 44 lb)
cards.text: No drain, no floor space and a simple button. The basket holds little, so ice is made as you use it.

cards.label: Undercounter (80 to 100 lb units)
cards.text: A bin stores a day of ice and the machine handles party loads. It needs floor space, ventilation and a drain plan.

howToChoose.note: Choose countertop for a few cups a day, and undercounter for hosting or a family that drinks ice all day.

rows: Refill a small tank by hand

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A bin that holds more than a basket, and an output rate that refills it within a few hours. Check the drain plan too.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 100 pound unit with a 25 pound capacity covers the biggest party, while the Costway handles a mid-sized gathering.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need a bin for more than twenty people or a true commercial duty cycle. A plumbed commercial unit with a larger bin is the next tier.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a few drinks a day, in which case the 44 pound countertop machine is plenty.

maintenance.why: Scale shortens evaporator life. Filtered water also keeps flavor clean.
It rinses the water path. Follow with a clean rinse before drinking ice.
Scale insulates the freezing surface. Use an approved descaler only.
Bins collect film in the corners. A dry cloth prevents mold.
A blocked drain backs water into the bin. Clear it before it overflows.

faq.q: Is an undercounter machine better than a countertop one?
faq.a: It is better for volume and storage, and worse for space and plumbing. A countertop unit is enough if you only need a few cups at a time.

faq.q: What does the $400 cap buy that lower caps do not?
faq.a: It buys 80 to 100 pound undercounter machines with insulated bins. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the live price before buying.
Most undercounter units want a drain or a pump for meltwater. The dual-inlet 100 pounder helps with supply, but you still need a plan for the drain.

faq.q: How long will an undercounter nugget machine last?
faq.a: Four to six years is realistic with filtered water and regular descaling. Compressors and augers are the main wear points.

faq.q: Does a bigger rating mean faster ice?
faq.a: Not directly. A larger evaporator makes more over a day but can take longer for the first batch. Check both numbers.

faq.q: Where can I put the machine?
faq.a: Leave space at the sides and back for airflow, and keep it away from heat. A garage works if temperatures stay moderate.
